findings.claim: Thresholds.__post_init__ (demo-repo/src/loanflow/config.py) currently validates exactly three invariants -- dti_low_max <= dti_medium_max, ltv_low_max <= ltv_medium_max, and 300 <= min_credit_score <= 850 -- raising loanflow.errors.ConfigError on violation of any of them.

Thresholds.__post_init__ has no check anywhere relating max_dti_hard_fail to dti_medium_max, or max_ltv_hard_fail to ltv_medium_max -- the entire method body (lines 22-28) contains only the three checks in F-1, and no other reference to max_dti_hard_fail or max_ltv_hard_fail exists anywhere else in demo-repo/src/loanflow/config.py.

findings.claim: DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS already satisfies max_dti_hard_fail >= dti_medium_max (0.50 >= 0.43) and max_ltv_hard_fail >= ltv_medium_max (1.00 >= 0.95); its literal field values are dti_low_max=0.36, dti_medium_max=0.43, ltv_low_max=0.80, ltv_medium_max=0.95, max_dti_hard_fail=0.50, max_ltv_hard_fail=1.00, min_credit_score=580, effective_date=2026-01-01.

Percentage (demo-repo/src/loanflow/primitives.py) is a frozen, order=True dataclass with a single integer field basis_points (validated non-negative in its own __post_init__), and it exposes total ordering (<, <=, >, >=, ==) via the dataclass order=True machinery operating on that integer field -- the same .basis_points integer attribute Thresholds.__post_init__'s existing checks already compare directly (self.dti_low_max.basis_points > self.dti_medium_max.basis_points), so any new hard-fail/medium invariant would compare .basis_points integers identically.

In underwriting_rules.py, both max_dti_rule and max_ltv_rule check the hard-fail comparison (profile value's basis_points > thresholds.max_*_hard_fail.basis_points) strictly before checking band membership (profile.dti_band is Band.HIGH / profile.ltv_band is Band.HIGH); consequently if a misconfigured Thresholds had max_dti_hard_fail's basis_points below dti_medium_max's basis_points (an inverted config), any DTI value strictly between the two thresholds would trip the first (hard-fail) branch and return early, and the borderline/high-band branch beneath it would never execute for that value -- the high-band/borderline outcome becomes unreachable for that range. The identical structure applies to max_ltv_rule with LTV/ltv_medium_max/max_ltv_hard_fail.

demo-repo/tests/unit/test_config.py currently contains no test covering the max_dti_hard_fail/dti_medium_max or max_ltv_hard_fail/ltv_medium_max relationship; the file's only tests are test_default_thresholds_are_valid (asserts min_credit_score), test_thresholds_rejects_inverted_dti_bounds (dti_low_max vs dti_medium_max), test_thresholds_rejects_inverted_ltv_bounds (ltv_low_max vs ltv_medium_max), and test_thresholds_rejects_out_of_range_credit_score -- the hard_fail fields appear only as fixed default values inside the _thresholds() helper (lines 18-19), never as an overridden/asserted value in any test body.
